key_insight: WEST is a scalable open-source platform that enables large excited-state simulations without explicitly computing virtual states, using GW, BSE, TDDFT, and embedding methods in one framework.
engineering_relevance: For perovskite solar-cell research, WEST can predict quasiparticle gaps, optical spectra, excitons, and excited-state forces at system sizes relevant to realistic defect and interface models.
method: Full-frequency GW, BSE, TDDFT, and quantum defect embedding in a common plane-wave pseudopotential framework
Density functional/density matrix perturbation theory plus low-rank dielectric and exact-exchange representations to reduce scaling
Hierarchical parallelization and GPU acceleration for near-ideal strong scaling to thousands of GPUs
evidence_signal: The abstract reports representative applications, including self-trapped excitons in metal-halide perovskites, and states the code scales to systems with more than a thousand atoms.
watch_item: Performance and accuracy depend on advanced HPC/GPU infrastructure and careful workflow setup, which may limit routine adoption for smaller groups.
paper_title: The WEST code for large-scale excited-state materials simulations
